ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: The study has been approved by the respective Ethics committees or Institutional Review Boards at the seven sites (UTA: #STUDY00004651; UIUC: #IRB24-1117; TCD: # SPREC022020-07; BCG: # 6497-B3002024000114; UZH: #KEK-ZH 2025-01839; UKT: #079/2024BO2; UR: #23-3580-101) and is compliant with US and European data protection regulations.
Written informed consent was obtained from every participant before any study procedure, in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki.

Of 820 individuals assessed for eligibility, 584 were enrolled between September 2024 and October 2025, and a complete record across questionnaires, audiometry and EEG was available for 562 of them (Figure 1c, Table S3).
table.formatted: Of 820 individuals assessed for eligibility, 584 were enrolled between September 2024 and October 2025, and a complete record across questionnaires, audiometry and EEG was available for 562 of them (Figure <ref type="figure" target="#fig_1">1c</ref>, Table <ref type="table">S3</ref>).

table.text: Participants were 18 to 70 years old [mean age of 45.4 (SD ± 16.1)] and 52% were female.

Because hyperacusis is tightly associated with severe tinnitus 51, it is possible that our exclusion criteria impacted the recruitment of participants that would have otherwise had clinically relevant tinnitus.
table.formatted: Because hyperacusis is tightly associated with severe tinnitus <ref type="bibr" target="#b50">51</ref> , it is possible that our exclusion criteria impacted the recruitment of participants that would have otherwise had clinically relevant tinnitus.

table.text: Written informed consent was obtained from every participant before any study procedure, in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki.
Participants were recruited to tertiary or academic tinnitus clinics and research centers via institutional emails, flyers, and journal announcements (Figure 1c).
table.formatted: Participants were recruited to tertiary or academic tinnitus clinics and research centers via institutional emails, flyers, and journal announcements (Figure <ref type="figure" target="#fig_1">1c</ref>).

table.text: Upon arrival at the clinical centers, participants received detailed information about the study procedures and provided written informed consent.

Eligible participants were aged 18 to 70 years, able to understand and consent to the research, cognitively unimpaired (Montreal Cognitive Assessment ≥ 26, presented only by certified researchers) and without hypersensitivity to sound (Hyperacusis Questionnaire ≤ 27; a score of 28 or above, the instrument's own threshold for hyperacusis, was exclusionary).
Less than 10% of the participants had acoustic trauma, acute or chronic otitis, or sudden hearing loss as a potential cause of their tinnitus.
Of 820 individuals assessed for eligibility, 236 were excluded and 584 were enrolled (Figure 1c, Table S3).
table.formatted: Of 820 individuals assessed for eligibility, 236 were excluded and 584 were enrolled (Figure <ref type="figure" target="#fig_1">1c</ref>, Table <ref type="table">S3</ref>).

power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: No significant cluster inhibition was found in 3 or 8 kHz NBN, likely due to the overlapping of PO and GP N100 responses in either group (Figure 2c). The pre-specified hypothesis was that inhibition would be reduced in tinnitus at narrowband carriers centered near the tinnitus percept and preserved with broadband noise. However, the observed pattern was the opposite whereby inhibition was reduced with the broadband carrier and did not differ between groups at either narrowband carrier. With 229 cases and 226 controls at the 3 kHz carrier and 232 cases and 223 controls at 8 kHz, an effect of d = 0.233 would have been detected with 80% power, so the narrowband null is unlikely to reflect insufficient sample size alone. These findings strongly support the notion that tinnitus correlates specifically with an impaired inhibition of cGPIAS in a BBN carrier.
table.header: Primary analysis: decreased inhibition in participants with tinnitus

table.text: In the analyzed sample of 232 cases and 223 controls, an effect of d = 0.233 would be detected with 80% power at a one-sided α of 0.05.

Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., *p* = .032) unless *p* values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use *p* < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., "decreased at the *p* < .05 significance threshold").

Written informed consent was obtained from every participant before any study procedure, in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki.
live_data_statements: Of 820 individuals assessed for eligibility, 584 were enrolled between September 2024 and October 2025, and a complete record across questionnaires, audiometry and EEG was available for 562 of them (Figure 1c, Table S3).
Participants were 18 to 70 years old [mean age of 45.4 (SD ± 16.1)] and 52% were female.

Because hyperacusis is tightly associated with severe tinnitus 51, it is possible that our exclusion criteria impacted the recruitment of participants that would have otherwise had clinically relevant tinnitus.
Written informed consent was obtained from every participant before any study procedure, in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki.
Participants were recruited to tertiary or academic tinnitus clinics and research centers via institutional emails, flyers, and journal announcements (Figure 1c).
Upon arrival at the clinical centers, participants received detailed information about the study procedures and provided written informed consent.

Eligible participants were aged 18 to 70 years, able to understand and consent to the research, cognitively unimpaired (Montreal Cognitive Assessment ≥ 26, presented only by certified researchers) and without hypersensitivity to sound (Hyperacusis Questionnaire ≤ 27; a score of 28 or above, the instrument's own threshold for hyperacusis, was exclusionary).
Less than 10% of the participants had acoustic trauma, acute or chronic otitis, or sudden hearing loss as a potential cause of their tinnitus.
Of 820 individuals assessed for eligibility, 236 were excluded and 584 were enrolled (Figure 1c, Table S3).
